NOTE NAMING
SPEED DRILLS
One-minute drills · treble, bass and alto clef · with answer keys and a progress chart
Grades 3–8 · 30 drill pages · answer keys

Teacher Notes

Note Naming Speed Drills · treble, bass and alto clef

How to use

  1. Hand out one drill and set a one-minute timer (a classroom clock or a phone is fine).
  2. Students write the letter name under each note and stop when time is called.
  3. Students check with the key (or swap with a partner), write the number correct in the score box and colour the bar on the progress chart.
  4. Repeat a drill another day: the same page, the same notes, a new score. Beating your own best is the point.

Each drill has 30 single notes in a 5 by 6 grid. Every note on a page is a new draw, so no two drills are the same. The answer is the letter name only (octave is not asked). Sharps and flats appear on drills 8–10 of each clef; no E♯, B♯, C♭ or F♭, and no naturals or double accidentals.

The ten levels (same in every clef)

#LevelWhat is on the page
1LinesOnly notes on the five lines.
2SpacesOnly notes in the four spaces.
3Lines and spacesEvery line and space of the staff.
4Just above and below the staffThe staff plus the space above and the space below.
5One ledger lineAdds the first ledger line above and below.
6Two ledger linesAdds the second ledger line above and below.
7Three ledger linesEvery ledger line up to three above and below.
8Sharps and flatsNotes in the staff, many with a sharp or a flat.
9Sharps, flats and ledger linesSharps, flats and up to two ledger lines.
10Mixed challengeEverything: lines, spaces, ledger lines, sharps and flats.

Where to start

ClefDrill pagesNotes
Treble clef7–16Drills 1–10. Keys on pages 37–38.
Bass clef17–26Drills 1–10. Keys on pages 39–40.
Alto clef27–36Drills 1–10. Keys on pages 41–42.

Grades 3–5 usually start with treble drills 1–5. Grades 6–8 use all three clefs: treble for band and orchestra, bass for low brass, low reeds, cello and bass, alto for viola. Alto clef: the C clef is centred on the middle line, which is middle C (C4).

Scoring bands on the student guide: 15 getting there, 20 solid, 25 fast, 30 lightning. Use them as personal goals, not grades.

Supports National Core Arts Standards, Music, Anchor Standard 4 (notation reading) as a fluency warm-up. No songs, lyrics or copyrighted characters are used. Contents: cover, teacher notes, student guide, clef reference, progress chart, drill log, 30 drills, 6 answer-key pages, terms.

How to Drill

A student guide: three clefs, one minute, beat your best
1 ReadyName and date. Pencil ready. Eyes on the first note, top left.
2 GoThe timer starts. Write each letter under its note, row by row.
3 StopPencils down when time is called. Draw a line after your last answer.
4 CheckUse the key. Count your correct answers and colour the progress chart.

Scoring

15Getting there
20Solid
25Fast
30Lightning

Only correct answers count. Do not rush into guesses: skip a note you are not sure of, finish the row, then go back.

Tricks that make you faster

  • Learn the lines and the spaces separately. Treble lines E G B D F (Every Good Boy Does Fine), spaces F A C E. Bass lines G B D F A (Good Boys Do Fine Always), spaces A C E G (All Cows Eat Grass). Alto lines F A C E G (Fat Alto Cats Eat Grass), spaces G B D F (Good Bears Dance Freely).
  • Use landmark notes. Treble: the G clef circles G. Bass: the two dots hug F. Alto: the middle line is C, the same pitch as middle C.
  • Count from a landmark for ledger lines: from the nearest line, step line, space, line, space.
  • Ledger lines. A short line through the note means the note sits on the line; a note with a short line just beyond it sits in the space next to it.
  • Sharps ♯ and flats ♭ go before the note and change the name: write F♯, B♭.

Your path

Each clef has ten drills. Start at drill 1, move on when you score 25 or more on a drill. The clef reference on the next page shows every note you will meet, with its name.

Clef Reference

Every note from the first ledger line below to the first ledger line above · middle C in orange
Treble clefmiddle C is on the first ledger line below the staff
Bass clefmiddle C is on the first ledger line above the staff
Alto clefmiddle C is on the middle line

Notes above and below these keep going up and down the alphabet: A B C D E F G, then start again. Sharps and flats raise or lower a note and keep its letter.
